title: STY/BUG Cleanup of quote marks and formatting in ase.db.sqlite
body:
Manual cleanup of quote marks in ase.db.sqlite

It is discouraged to use double-quotes inside sqlite statements, and officially unsupported (by default) for recent versions.

Some users/developers have reported errors related to the use of double-quote marks in sqlite statements, but they are proving difficult to reproduce in a clean environment. #1746 

In the ASE codebase it is standard to quote strings with single-quotes.

In the context of this file, which was mostly quoted with double-quotes, the ASE convention should be to use single-quotes _unless_ the string contains a SQL statement with a quoted string: in such cases the python string should use double quotes and the SQL statement use single-quotes internally. With a consistent style in the rest of the file, this helps these strings to stand out slightly as having an interesting quote property.

comments.author: ajjackson
comments.body: With the quote marks consistent, and a bit of "boy scout principle" modernisation of some format statements to f-strings... I might as well run `ruff format` as well and get it all consistent.

comments.author: ajjackson
comments.body: Do you think it would be appropriate to do a release note that "this may fix sqlite errors under certain undefined conditions" or just gloss over that? I wouldn't generally add a release note for formatting changes but here they seem to _actually_ matter.

comments.author: ajjackson
comments.body: I'd be happy to merge this as-is but leave #1746 open a bit longer to see if it helps that user. Even if not, it's a worthy style update :sweat_smile:

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
Either don't mention in changelog or something very short like `Fix deprecated SQL syntax.`, after all it's not just formatting.

I'd just close the issue and say "Please reopen if the problem is nevertheless not resolved".
